annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "Guinness" on page 35 ("The Encounter in Phoenix Park"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within HCE's mysterious sin in Phoenix Park, the spread of gossip through Dublin, and the Cad with the pipe. During this Age of Gods phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
Gordon, John. Finnegans Blog (Tavern chapters). https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com

annotations.annotation_text: HCE manifestation "Earwicker" on page 35 within "The Encounter in Phoenix Park": here the universal father-figure Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker appears in the context of HCE's mysterious sin in Phoenix Park, the spread of gossip through Dublin, and the Cad with the pipe. During this Age of Gods phase, HCE embodies the patriarch whose guilt, grandeur, and fall drive the cyclical dream forward.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
McHugh, Roland. The Sigla of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/siglaoffinnegans0000mchu
James Joyce Digital Archive: Finnegans Wake Notons. https://jjda.ie
